questions.q: Where does Oracle store the master encryption key used by TDE?
options: In an external keystore (wallet), outside the database itself
Inside the SYSTEM tablespace
In the unified_audit_trail view
Inside the data dictionary, alongside user passwords
questions.explain: The wallet/keystore is deliberately external, so a copy of the data files alone can't be decrypted.

questions.q: What's the tradeoff between a password-protected keystore and an auto-login keystore?
options: Auto-login opens automatically so the database can start without manual intervention, trading some security for availability
There is no difference; both require manual opening after every restart
Auto-login keystores can't be used with tablespace encryption
Password-protected keystores don't support AES256
questions.explain: Password-protected keystores must be opened manually after a restart; auto-login opens itself, at some security cost.

questions.q: Why is tablespace encryption generally preferred over column encryption for new work?
options: It's simpler to administer — every object in the tablespace is encrypted automatically, rather than tracking individual encrypted columns
Column encryption was removed from modern Oracle versions
Tablespace encryption doesn't require a wallet
Column encryption doesn't support AES256
questions.explain: Tablespace encryption is a one-time setting instead of a per-column decision, and avoids some of column encryption's indexing restrictions.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT protected by TDE, per this lesson?
options: Data moving across the network to a client, and data sitting decrypted in the buffer cache while the instance runs
Data files at rest on disk
Backups taken of encrypted data files
A stolen or decommissioned drive containing the data files
questions.explain: TDE protects data at rest; network transit is covered separately by Oracle Native Network Encryption, and in-memory data is decrypted while the instance runs.

questions.q: A user has legitimate SELECT privilege on a TDE-encrypted table. What do they see when they query it?
options: Plaintext, the same as always — TDE doesn't replace access control
An encrypted blob they must decrypt manually
An error, since encrypted tables can't be queried normally
Only the columns that aren't encrypted
questions.explain: TDE defends against someone bypassing the database entirely (e.g. reading raw data files); it doesn't change what an authorized session sees.
